[00:00] Priya Desai: good morning everyone, thanks for making time. i'm Priya, account lead at Redwood, with Ethan who will run the demo. goal: show hosted generation basics, streaming transport knobs, and recommended retry/backoff patterns.
[00:10] Sofia Martinez: hi, thanks. our product needs low-latency short replies for in-app prompts, so p95 is important. we'll also want a fallback plan for peak hours.
[00:18] Ethan Liu: hey team, i'll start by firing a streaming chat call from the Console sandbox so you can see partial tokens arriving. excuse my keyboard noise.

[00:30] [clicks, a short pause]
[00:36] Ethan Liu: streaming live now. note the UI shows chunks arriving roughly every 80-120ms depending on chunk_size and model. by default Redwood bundles tokens into groups rather than single-character streams.
[01:02] Liam O'Connor: i see it in the shared console. there's some jitter on first chunk, is that normal?
[01:08] Ethan Liu: yes, time-to-first-chunk depends on model warmness and whether prefix/KV cache hits. smaller chunk_size reduces time-to-first-chunk but increases per-token overhead; it's a tradeoff.

[01:30] Jaya Singh: can you spell out recommended defaults for chat UX? we want deterministic short answers.
[01:35] Ethan Liu: for predictable short answers we usually recommend: max_tokens around 40-80, temperature 0.0-0.25, top_p 0.8-0.95, and chunk_size small (like 4-8 tokens) so UI gets early bytes. also set a hard client timeout slightly above the expected SLO.

[02:05] Sofia Martinez: when a stream disconnects mid-response, what's the recommended client flow? immediate retry or resume?
[02:11] Priya Desai: good Q. Redwood supports resume tokens in the stream and server-side KV prefix caching. typical pattern: attempt a resume using resume token; if not possible, re-send user message with same client-side idempotency key and let the service detect duplicate. avoid immediate hammering; use exponential backoff with jitter.

[02:40] Ethan Liu: i'll inject a transient error in the sandbox so you can see how a client would observe it.
[02:46] [typing, brief silence]
[02:52] Ethan Liu: injected error; stream disconnected and SDK logs show an error with code (transient). our SDK example does: wait backoff, then retry with same idempotency_key or resume_token. i'll paste the snippet in chat.

[03:20] Liam O'Connor: do you expose whether a response was partial in headers or metadata? we need to decide on UI fallback behavior.

[03:27] Ethan Liu: yes, responses include metadata flags and a partial/final marker. plus a small resume token payload to restart where left off if possible. note that transcript tooling may occasionally spell KV cache as 'K-Vcach' in older auto-transcripts, so ignore odd spellings in docs.

[03:55] Jaya Singh: about retries: what concrete backoff policy do you recommend? we want to avoid amplifying load.

[04:02] Priya Desai: recommended: cap retries to 3 attempts, exponential backoff (base 200-500ms), and add full jitter. for single-turn non-chat calls, use idempotency keys to enable safe retries. for chat flows where history grows, prefer resume tokens and re-sending the user's prompt rather than blindly replaying server-side state.

[04:35] Sofia Martinez: how does batching affect p95? our traffic is spiky at 9am and 5pm.

[04:42] Ethan Liu: Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching and will trade throughput for latency based on the configured latency SLO. for strict p95 targets you can reduce batch windows or use reserved capacity/burst policies; we can also pin low-batch windows on hosted for critical routes.

[05:10] Liam O'Connor: we prefer hosted but can't tolerate long tails. any middle ground?

[05:16] Priya Desai: yes, hosted with reserved burst capacity is common: you stay on hosted control plane but reserve GPU pools for your tenant during peak hours. plus route fallbacks let you degrade to quantized variants automatically when queue depth or latency thresholds exceed limits.

[05:40] Jaya Singh: can you demo route fallback?

[05:45] Ethan Liu: opening route policies. here's a rule: prefer low-latency variant A, but if queue depth > 50 or p95 exceeds 400ms, route to quantized variant B. you can also route by geo so EU traffic stays in-region.

[06:12] Sofia Martinez: region pinning is important  we have European data residency constraints. how does that work on hosted?

[06:18] Priya Desai: hosted supports region pins and we can limit logs/trace retention to region. for strict residency and airgapped needs we offer Private deployment. hosted can work for most regulated customers if we agree on KMS and retention policies.

[06:45] Liam O'Connor: on security, do you provide customer-managed keys and SSO?

[06:50] Priya Desai: yes: SSO via SAML, RBAC in the Console, audit logs, and optional customer-managed KMS. i'll include SOC2 and KMS integration docs in the follow-up.

[07:10] Jaya Singh: cost question  rough math for 2k DAUs, avg 8 turns, 40 tokens per turn?

[07:17] Ethan Liu: quick estimate: roughly 2k * 8 * 40 = 640k tokens/day. with caching and prefix hits you often see 10-30% savings. we'll produce three scenarios (standard hosted, hosted with caching, and quantized variant) and attach a spreadsheet.

[07:50] Sofia Martinez: what about SDKs for mobile streaming (iOS/Android)? we need sample patterns.

[07:56] Ethan Liu: we have mobile SDK examples using SSE and websockets. mobile platforms sometimes need token coalescing to avoid small-packet overhead. i'll include those repos in the follow-up.

[08:20] Jaya Singh: any known pitfalls migrating from our current vendor?

[08:26] Priya Desai: common items: mapping auth flows (we support API keys and OAuth), aligning idempotency key semantics, adding resume tokens, and adjusting client timeouts. we can provide a migration checklist and small shim to minimize changes.

[08:55] Ethan Liu: quick live test: i'll paste a short FAQ summarization prompt and stream the result.

[09:18] Sofia Martinez: output ok, but a small hallucination there about a product name. how do you mitigate hallucinations?

[09:24] Priya Desai: multiple levers: lower temperature, stronger prompt constraints, output filters, or choose a model variant with stronger grounding. Redwood also supports evaluation hooks so you can run automated checks on pilot outputs.

[09:50] Liam O'Connor: pilot process? we'd like a 2-week pilot to validate p95 and cost.

[09:56] Priya Desai: perfect. standard pilot: Redwood provisions a pilot environment, enables detailed tracing and metrics, and we agree on a small benchmark test plan. Ethan will provide the script to run.
